messages:
Sam (Product): quick sync — we need to reconcile a few launch tradeoffs before we give GA a greenlight. TL;DR: SLA windows, docs gaps, oncall escalation, monitoring alerts, and pricing banding. who's got immediate ownership?

Morgan (Eng): happy to own the SLA targets + perf experiments. can we lock p50/p95/p99 numbers and what to do if quantized model regresses?

Anya (SRE): I can take monitoring & alert playbooks. need a final list of critical metrics (latency, error-rate, queue-depth, mem-evicts). also want runbook templates for two outage modes: degraded throughput and OOM.

Jesse (Support): Support will own tiered escalation + troubleshooting matrix. need sample failure flows and a PDF quickstart for tier-1 to reference. also request a short training session before GA.

Olivia (Finance): pricing bins need a decision. we proposed three tiers (dev/scale/enterprise). we need usage thresholds for autoscale bursts and an expected unit-cost delta for quantized vs full models.

Sam (Product): action items I see: Morgan SLA targets, Anya monitoring + runbooks, Jesse support doc & training, Olivia finalize price thresholds. timeline: get drafts by EOD Wed, review Thu. OK?

Morgan (Eng): okay — propose SLA: p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 650ms for hosted baseline. fallback variants allowed but must be explicit in routing policy. I'll add regression gating for any quantized rollout.

Anya (SRE): monitoring list: token-emit-rate, request-latency-hist, kv-cache-hit, gpu-mem-usage, queue-time, model-fallback-rate. alert severity mapping: sev1 (total availability < 99.5%), sev2 (p99 breach > 10m), sev3 (sustained p95 degradation). I'll draft runbooks with play steps and runbook links.

Jesse (Support): for training: 30m walkthrough + canned playbook zip. I'll draft the troubleshooting matrix: "cache miss spike -> clear prefix cache" and "OOM -> scale pool or fallback to CPU pool". also want a one-pager for sales team.

Olivia (Finance): we'll set thresholds: dev < 1M tokens/month, scale 1M–50M, enterprise > 50M. bursting: allow 2x for short windows (configurable), with overage billing. need estimate of cost delta for 4-bit quant vs 16-bit — can eng give per-token cost estimate?

Morgan (Eng): I'll run cost sims and post numbers. rough immediate estimate: quantized path ~0.45x unit-cost vs baseline at typical seq lengths. will produce a simple table.

Sam (Product): docs-wise: product docs need a "What changes at GA" section (SLA, billing, migration notes), plus a short "Known limitations" bullet list. Also want a short customer-facing FAQ for the rollout. Can someone own the GA announcement draft?

Jesse (Support): I'll own the customer FAQ + internal tl;dr. also will schedule support training Wed afternoon.

Anya (SRE): small ask: add canary policy to the rollouts doc. we should require 24h canary with automated rollback on p99 spikes. deploy-bot: any constraints from pipeline?

deploy-bot: Canary pipelines available. current default canary window: 6h. Manual approvals required for production scale > 2 nodes.

Sam (Product): OK change to 24h canary + automated rollback if p99 > 2x baseline for 15m. Morgan: can you wire that into the rollout config?

Morgan (Eng): yes. will add config snippet in repo and a short example: ```yaml
rollout:
  canary_window: 24h
  rollback_condition:
    metric: p99_latency
    multiplier: 2.0
    window: 15m
```

Olivia (Finance): once we have unit-cost sims I'll draft the final pricing note and runway impact. deadline for legal/redlines? friday COB ideally.

Sam (Product): summary of owners and deadlines: Morgan (SLAs + rollout config) EOD Wed, Anya (monitoring + runbooks) EOD Wed, Jesse (support docs + training) Wed afternoon, Olivia (pricing note) Thu EOD, Sam to consolidate announcement Thu. We'll reconvene Thu 10am to sign off. Anything else?

Jesse (Support): please add a short example customer incident scenario to the runbooks — makes training much easier.

Anya (SRE): noted. I'll include two scenarios.

Sam (Product): thanks all — I'll spin up the review PR after receive drafts. :thumbsup:
